chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from Salih ibn al-Sindi al-Jammal, from the one he mentioned, from Karram ibn 'Amr, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Karram: When you intend to go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), visit him while you are sorrowful, grief-stricken, disheveled, and covered with dust, for indeed al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed while he was sorrowful, grief-stricken, disheveled, covered with dust, hungry, and thirsty.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended spiritual and physical demeanor for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the concept of *mura'at al-hal* (mirroring the state) in ziyarah, where the pilgrim’s external demeanor reflects the internal and physical reality of the Imam at the moment of martyrdom. Scholarly tradition interprets the specific descriptors—disheveled hair, dust, hunger, and thirst—not merely as literal conditions but as profound symbols of the cosmic injustice and spiritual isolation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), thereby transforming the visit into an empathetic reenactment of his sacrifice.
